div.head: EGu 11
div.ab: Gif wiccan oððe wigleras, mansworan oððe morðwyrhtan oððe fule, afylede, æbære horcwenan ahwar on lande wurðan agytene, ðonne fyse hi man of earde ⁊ clænsie þa ðeode, oððe on earde forfare hy mid ealle, buton hig geswican ⁊ þe deoppor gebetan.

Gyf wycan oððe wigleras, monsworan oððe morðwyrhtan oððe fule, afylede, æbære horcwenan ahwar on lande wurðan agytene, ðonne fyse hi man of earde ⁊ clænsie þa ðeode, oððon on earde forfare hy mid ealle, buton hig geswican ⁊ ðe deoppor gebetan.

Si wyce uel wigleres, mansƿoran et morðwirthan ⁊ fule, afylede, abere horcƿenan alicubi sint in terra inuente, educantur de patria, et emundetur populus, uel in patria dispereant omnino, nisi cessent et profundius emendent.

[Be wicum, wiglerum, mansworum etc.] Gif wiccan oðð wigleras, mansworan oððe morðwyrhtan oððe fule, afylede, æbere horcwenan ahwar on lande wurðan agytene, ðonne fyse hi man of earde ⁊ clænsie þa ðeode, oððe on earde forfare hy mid ealle, buton hig geswican ⁊ þe deoppor gebetan.

Gif wiccan oððe wigleras, mansworan oððe morðwyrhtan oððe fule, afylede, æbære horcwenan ahwar on lande wurðan agytene, ðonne fyse hi man of earde and clænsie þa ðeode, oððe on earde forfare hy mid ealle buton hig geswican and þe deoppor gebetan.

(Von Zauberern, Wahrsagern, Meineidigen etc. Ld) Wenn Zauberer oder Wahrsager, Meineidige oder heimliche Mordstifter oder schmutzige, verderbte, offenbare Hurenweiber irgendwo im Lande betroffen werden, dann jage man sie ausser Landes und säubere das Volk, oder man vernichte sie gänzlich im Lande, es sei denn, sie lassen [vom Bösen] ab und büssen um so tiefer.

(Of sorcerers, soothsayers, perjurers, etc. Ld) If sorcerers or soothsayers, perjurers or secret murderers, or filthy, corrupt, notorious whores are found anywhere in the land, then let them be driven out of the country and the people cleansed, or let them be destroyed utterly in the land, unless they desist [from evil] and make all the deeper amends.

If wizards or sorcerers, perjurers or they who secretly compass death, or vile, polluted, notorious prostitutes be met with anywhere in the country, they shall be driven from the land and the nation shall be purified; otherwise they shall be utterly destroyed in the land—unless they cease from their wickedness and make amends to the utmost of their ability.

If magicians or wizards, perjurers or murderers, or foul, corrupted, notorious prostitutes come to be discovered anywhere in the land, then they must be expelled from the country and the realm cleansed, or from the country they must be utterly wiped out unless they desist and repent most deeply.

Nicht Totschläger oder offene Mörder; vgl. Gl Mord 2. a. 4. Zu eng, nicht falsch (vgl. Gl Giftmischerei 1), venefici (-cæ, wieder Fem. II Cn 4a Q), malefici In Cn. Das Verstohlene drückt richtig aus latrones-homicidae Cons Cn

Not killers or open murderers; cf. Gl Mord 2. a. 4. Too narrow, though not wrong (cf. Gl Giftmischerei 1), are venefici (-cæ, again feminine, II Cn 4a Q) and malefici In Cn. The secrecy is correctly expressed by latrones-homicidae Cons Cn

‘Ehebrecherinnen’ Price, Toller, nach Gotischem und Nordischem. Zu Tollers Zitaten passt aber überall ‘Hure’; auch in Wulfstans Hom. steht æwbrecan gesondert vor horing (Sweet Agsa. reader 253); Glossen haben meretrix. Freilich steht bei II Cn 6 in einem Gesetz gleichen Inhalts æwbrecan an dieser Stelle in derselben Gesellschaft. Gewerbsmässige Huren gab es um 890; Asser 96 ed. Stevenson p. 83. Vgl. Gl Unzucht 12. a

‘Adulteresses’ Price, Toller, on the analogy of Gothic and Norse. But ‘whore’ fits Toller’s quotations throughout; in Wulfstan’s Hom. too æwbrecan stands separately before horing (Sweet Agsa. reader 253); glosses have meretrix. Admittedly, at II Cn 6, in a law of the same content, æwbrecan stands at this point in the same company. Professional whores existed c. 890; Asser 96 ed. Stevenson p. 83. Cf. Gl Unzucht 12. a
Vgl. ebd. 1c; Strafe 10e; Brunner II 587. — Q braucht emundare auch sonst; vgl. Wb
Cf. ibid. 1c; Strafe 10e; Brunner II 587. — Q uses emundare elsewhere too; cf. Wb

Quadr. translates Si sortilege uel incantatrices, etc. Wiccan may be either masculine or feminine, but wigleras must be masculine. With this law may be compared a passage in Wulfstan’s Sermo ad Anglos (printed in Sweet’s Anglo-Saxon Reader, 8th Ed. p. 95): and her syndan manswaran and morðorwyrhtan, and her syndan hadbrecan and æwbrecan,...and her syndan wiccan and wælcerian, etc.

Birch, Cart. Sax. 1131 affords an interesting comparison. It describes how land at Ailsworth had belonged to a widow and her son who practised pinsticking witchcraft upon Ælsie; but she was drowned at London Bridge and her son was outlawed: ⁊ þæt land æt Ægeleswyrðe headde an wyduwe ⁊ hire sune ær forwyrt for þan þe hi drifon iserne stacan on Ælsie Wulfstanes feder ⁊ þæt werð æreafe ⁊ man teh þæt morð forð of hire inclifan. Þa nam man þæt wif ⁊ adrencte hi æt Lundene brigce, ⁊ hire sune ætberst ⁊ werð utlah, etc.
